trust_decision.summary: At dial time, FetchAndEncodeURL resolves the request-supplied host and trusts isPublicIP's verdict on every resolved address, refusing the fetch unless all are public; the trust decision is a hand-written address deny-list, not a positive allow-list.

landing_point.why: The advisory names isPublicIP by name; anyone reading the summary opens this function first and sees one netip predicate chain with no CGNAT, no IPv6-transition unwrapping and no fec0::/10 case.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /v1/chat/completions (Bedrock image_url and file.url document blocks; Vertex-Anthropic file.url document blocks) and POST /v1/responses (Bedrock image_url via responses.go:3264,4251) -> FetchAndEncodeURL
fix_sites.module_kind: core provider-utils library (internal Go package, module github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ConfigureDialer's deny-list guards operator-configured provider base URLs over the fasthttp transport, and it deliberately permits loopback plus (with AllowPrivateNetwork) RFC 1918 for self-hosted providers such as Ollama/vLLM/SGL, so it reads as an intentionally narrower legacy path that the fetch.go advisory never covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Public IPv4 reached through 6to4 or NAT64 must remain fetchable (NAT64 is the normal path from IPv6-only clusters to the IPv4 internet); the correct fix unwraps the embedded IPv4 and re-checks it rather than blocking 2002::/16 or 64:ff9b::/96 wholesale, so an over-broad prefix block breaks legitimate public fetches (the fix's own test keeps 2002:0808:0808:: allowed).

O6_input_shapes: NAT64 well-known 64:ff9b::/96 carrying an IPv4 in bytes 12..15
NAT64 local-use 64:ff9b:1::/48 with RFC 6052 u-octet skipped (bytes 6,7,9,10)
hostname form resolved by net.Resolver versus a bracketed IPv6 literal in the URL

O8_uncovered_routes.route: All provider outbound traffic (including user-chosen provider base URLs saved through POST /api/providers) goes through the fasthttp dial closure, whose deny-list uses network.IsPrivateIP and has no CGNAT, 6to4/NAT64 unwrapping or fec0::/10 case.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Base URLs are operator configuration, not request input, and the path intentionally allows loopback and RFC 1918 for local providers.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the fix, different transport (fasthttp) and different public function; shared classifier in core/network

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Shared lower-level classifier network.IsPrivateIP (used by both ValidateExternalURL and ConfigureDialer) returns false for CGNAT, 6to4/NAT64-wrapped internal IPv4 and fec0::/10.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a generic 'private address' helper with its own callers, not the SSRF check named in the advisory; hardening it would also change provider connectivity policy.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package away (core/network), reached only through callers

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Pricing URL is fetched with a bare http.Client (no dial-time IP check) after only a save-time ValidateExternalURL(..., allowPrivateNetwork=true) that skips loopback entirely.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Pricing is operator-supplied framework configuration fetched at startup, and the save-time validator is the intended control for it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate Go module (framework), different package, different client stack (net/http with default transport)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Model-parameters URL takes the same bare-client path with only save-time ValidateExternalURL.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same config-not-input argument; a neighbouring feature to pricing sync.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: single file from the pricing route, framework module

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Admin config save performs a server-side GET of the submitted PricingURL/ModelParametersURL with a bare http.Client after ValidateExternalURL(rawURL, true), which passes loopback, CGNAT and 6to4/NAT64-wrapped internal addresses.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Admin-only endpoint whose whole purpose is to probe reachability, so it looks intentional that it is not locked down like the model-facing fetcher.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module (transports) and different package from the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Provider base-URL validation on create/update goes through ValidateExternalURL, which skips loopback and never unwraps IPv6 transition addresses.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: loopback is skipped by design for local deployments and AllowPrivateNetwork is an explicit opt-in, so the weakness looks like intended policy.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (core root package bifrost) from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second 'is this address internal?' classifier kept next to the subnet table
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The tree already carries two address classifiers (fetch.go's netip predicate chain and network.IsPrivateIP over net.IP), so a maintainer hardening one and not the other is exactly the drift we see here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A dial-time guard for the fasthttp provider clients that must stay loopback-permissive
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every provider constructs its client through ConfigureProxy/ConfigureDialer/ConfigureTLS, so a security fix author would plausibly add the check there and then have to keep local providers working.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-provider URL inliner wrapper (sanitize image URL, then fetch)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Providers whose upstream only accepts inline bytes each grew their own inliner, so a new provider would get a copy of this wrapper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A config-URL loader that fetches with a plain http.Client and relies on the save-time validator
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pricing/model-parameters loaders already do this twice in one file, so a third loader is a natural extension.

O9_family: CWE-918 server-side request forgery via an incomplete IP deny-list (CGNAT, IPv6 transition addresses, deprecated site-local)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26.3 declared in core/go.mod; multi-module workspace by convention (core, framework, transports, plugins, cli each have their own go.mod and there is no go.work), so each module builds and tests independently
O10_build.project_tests: core/providers/utils/dialer_test.go (TestConfigureDialer_SSRFProtection, _SSRFProxyBypass, _SSRFZeroTimeout, _SSRFMultiIPAllFail), core/utils_test.go (TestValidateExternalURL, TestIsPrivateIP), transports/bifrost-http/handlers/utils_test.go (checkURLAccessibility); the fix adds a new core/providers/utils/fetch_test.go (TestIsPublicIP) which does not exist at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Block 100.64.0.0/10, 2002::/16, 64:ff9b::/96 and fec0::/10 inside isPublicIP only, which both kills legitimate public 6to4/NAT64 targets and leaves network.IsPrivateIP, the ConfigureDialer dial path and the pricing/config URL fetchers unhardened.

out_of_scope_notes: Sighted outside this advisory's scope and not pursued: the pricing/model-parameters loaders accept file:// URLs and read arbitrary local paths (framework/modelcatalog/sync.go:124-128, :508-512) and checkURLAccessibility stats arbitrary local files (transports/bifrost-http/handlers/config.go:994-1002); these are path/host-file reads, a different weakness family from the SSRF deny-list.
